title: POC scoping - Orchid Logic integration planning
summary: AE+SE (Redwood) and Orchid Logic engineering discussed POC goals, expected workload, benchmark plan, and integration approach. Primary success criteria: p95 latency <200ms for typical 80-120 token responses on hosted/Dedicated fallback, deterministic structured JSON outputs for downstream processing, and a measurable cost/throughput baseline. Action items: Redwood to provide SDK snippets, OpenAI-compatible endpoint examples, security docs, and a benchmark runbook. Orchid to provide sample prompts, a representative dataset, and access window for SRE benchmarking.
next_steps: Redwood to send POC statement of work and pricing sheet by 2027-06-21
Redwood SE to share SDK example (Node/Python) and OpenAI-compatible endpoint snippets (link) by EOD 2027-06-19
Orchid to share sample prompt set and 10k-message representative payload by 2027-06-22
Schedule benchmark run (week of 2027-06-28) - Redwood SE + Orchid SRE
Security: Redwood to share SOC2 + infra diagram + KMS integration notes by 2027-06-23
action_items: Priya Nair (Redwood SE): prepare benchmark runbook + perf script - due 2027-06-24
Alex Reyes (Redwood AE): send SOW + pricing + trial credits - due 2027-06-21
Jordan Kim (Orchid Eng Lead): provide canonical prompt set and sample logs - due 2027-06-22
Liam O'Neill (Orchid SRE): reserve a 4-hour window for testbed and confirm VPC access - due 2027-06-25
transcript:
Date: 2027-06-18 10:00 PDT / 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Orchid Eng Lead), Maya Singh (CTO), Liam O'Neill (SRE)

[00:00] Alex Reyes: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, i'm alex from Redwood - quick roll call?
[00:10] Jordan Kim: jordan here, maya and liam with me. thanks for organizing.
[00:15] Priya Nair: hey all, priya from the SE team. i'll drive the benchmarks and integration plan.
[00:25] Maya Singh: thanks, we'll cover high level goals first.

Summary / Objectives (auto): define POC success criteria, confirm workload sizing (qps, seq len), plan benchmark runs, and agree SDK/openai-compatible integration approach + timeline.

[02:05] Alex Reyes: quick context - redwood offers hosted api, dedicated capacity, and private vpc options. for the pilot most customers start hosted to validate functional behavior then we run perf on dedicated. does that match your expectation?
[02:25] Jordan Kim: yes, we wanted to start hosted but need a path to VPC or dedicated because of data residency and lower jitter on p95.
[02:40] Maya Singh: also need predictable costs if we go to prod.

[04:12] Priya Nair: great — let's get into success criteria. from our side what would make this POC a win? typical asks: latency p95 target, throughput target, and structured output accuracy for our downstream parsing.
[04:30] Jordan Kim: for us, primary: p95 < 200ms for ~100 token outputs at our expected concurrency, second: output must conform to JSON schema with >95% parse accuracy, and third: cost less than our current OpEx baseline - we use OpenAI and are paying close to $X/token.
[05:02] Alex Reyes: got it. when you say concurrency, what's your peak qps?
[05:10] Jordan Kim: our peak front-end qps for user-facing suggestions is ~120 rps, steady-state 30-50 rps; but POC we can test at 50, 100, 150 to see scaling.
[05:30] Priya Nair: good, that maps to a few bench vectors: single-request latency tests, steady-state throughput, and burst tests with higher concurrency. we'll also instrument batching and caching behavior.

[06:15] Maya Singh: sequence lengths - most outputs are 60-140 tokens, prompts average 180 tokens. we do some multi-turn but for the POC single-turn generation is fine.

[07:00] Priya Nair: perfect. for benchmarks we propose: (1) p95 latency microbench at 1-10 concurrency; (2) throughput run at 50/100/150 rps for 10 mins each; (3) structured output validation using your schema with a scoring script; (4) cost calc for tokens + infra estimate. does that sound ok?
[07:25] Jordan Kim: yes. also want to test function/tool calling - we rely on tool invocation to fetch company data. can you support OpenAI-style function calling or a webhook-based tool hook?
[07:40] Priya Nair: yes — redwood supports OpenAI-compatible endpoints and function/tool calling. note some transcription in our docs shows "OpenAI compatiable" occasionally, but we do have examples. we'll share the SDK snippets.

[08:30] Alex Reyes: big question is integration surface: you have an existing service that hits OpenAI? is that right?
[08:40] Jordan Kim: yeah, currently our backend calls OpenAI chat completions via their API; we have an adapter layer so switching endpoints is mostly config, but we do need same request/response shapes.
[08:55] Priya Nair: perfect. Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoint accepts chat completions + function call schema. we also provide structured output helpers - you can opt into JSON-schema-enforced outputs. we'll share a Node and Python SDK example.

[10:15] Liam O'Neill: on security - we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), KMS support for customer-managed keys, and audit logs retained 90 days. do you support that on private/dedicated?
[10:35] Alex Reyes: yes, private and dedicated support KMS, SAML, RBAC, and we can provide audit logs. hosted has standard encryption at rest; for managed keys you go dedicated/private. we'll attach our security pack.

[12:00] Maya Singh: about deterministic structured outputs - we need >95% successful parses into our schema. how do you measure that?
[12:12] Priya Nair: we'll run a structured output validation test: send your prompt set, evaluate against schema, and report parse rate plus typical failure modes. we can also recommend temperature/stop token settings and sampling params to improve determinism.

[14:00] Jordan Kim: benchmarks: what hardware will you run the dedicated perf on for the POC?
[14:10] Priya Nair: for fairness we'll run hosted baseline (our managed fleet) then a dedicated pool using A100-ish hardware in the region you prefer, plus a small on-prem emulator if needed. we'll define model variant - typically an open model comparable to what you're using.
[14:35] Alex Reyes: important to note: batching and KV-cache behaviour can change p95 for short responses. we'll test with and without batching and with our prefix cache enabled for repeated prompts.

[16:00] Jordan Kim: can you do streaming? we sometimes stream tokens to the client for perceived latency improvements.
[16:10] Priya Nair: yes streaming supported. we'll include stream and non-stream scenarios in the runbook.

[18:30] Maya Singh: timeline - we want a 4-week POC. week 1: integration + sanity, week 2: benchmark runs, week 3: iterate on prompts and fallback policies, week 4: evaluation + SOW decision. is that realistic?
[18:50] Alex Reyes: yes that aligns with what we usually do. we can compress if you have engineering bandwidth.

[21:00] Priya Nair: for the SDK examples i will share a repo snippet showing OpenAI-compatible calls, function calling examples, and structured output schema enforcement. link will be in the SOW email.

[23:10] Jordan Kim: on cost - we need a per-1M token estimate for hosted vs dedicated and an ops estimate for dedicated.
[23:25] Alex Reyes: i'll include both pricing bands in the SOW; during the POC we'll provide billing telemetry so you can calculate projected monthly costs.

[25:40] Maya Singh: any blockers on our side? we need VPC peering for the SRE-run benchmarks and a data sample for structured output testing.
[25:52] Liam O'Neill: i'll open a ticket to get that sample and confirm peering windows.

[27:00] Priya Nair: action items recap - we need the prompt set and sample payload. Redwood will prep the perf scripts and a short runbook that lists request shapes, headers, and example responses (including function call examples).

[30:00] Alex Reyes: quick demo of an SDK snippet (screen share narr): shows how to call redwood openai-compatible endpoint, include function definition payload, and parse the returned "tool_call" hook - notes that naming may appear as "K-V cash" in earlier transcripts but that is just a transcription issue.

[35:00] Jordan Kim: small nit - we have an internal parsing pipeline that insists on strict JSON; can you support response-in-json only mode and no additional commentary?
[35:15] Priya Nair: yes we support forced JSON output via schema enforcement and can also set temperature to 0 and use stop tokens. we'll include recommended params in the runbook.

[40:00] Liam O'Neill: SRE question: for high-concurrency throughput tests, how do you simulate user identity/tenant isolation?
[40:12] Priya Nair: we can parameterize calls with API keys to emulate tenants; for dedicated we can route by policy and we also support per-customer rate limits.

[45:00] Maya Singh: what's the rollback/fallback plan if you see regressions in quality when we switch from hosted to dedicated or different model quantization?
[45:12] Alex Reyes: we recommend canary rollout + A/B tests; Redwood supports automatic fallback to a compatible model variant (higher precision) on increased error rates. we'll instrument quality metrics tied to eval prompts so you can detect regressions quickly.

[50:20] Jordan Kim: okay timeline/agreement - next steps and due dates?
[50:30] Alex Reyes: we'll email SOW/pricing and SDK links. schedule bench week of 6/28 - priya will lead runs.

[55:00] Maya Singh: good. any final questions?
[55:10] Jordan Kim: none from me. thanks everyone.
[55:20] Liam O'Neill: thanks. i'll confirm VPC timings.
[55:30] Alex Reyes: thanks folks we'll follow up with the artifacts and the benchmark runbook.
[56:00] Priya Nair: thanks all.

Recap / Close: POC scoped to 4 weeks with explicit perf runs and structured output validation; Redwood to provide SDK snippets, SOW, pricing, and security docs; Orchid to provide prompt set, sample payloads, and SRE access window for benchmarking.

References/links mentioned: SOW template (link in email), SDK examples repo: https://redwood.ai/sdks (example), security pack doc link to be shared via SOW.
